title: Jerk Chicken
shortDescription: Island heat that still feeds eight
subtitle: Island heat that still feeds eight
description: Island heat that still feeds eight. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Season under the skin
steps.instruction: Dry chicken thoroughly. Season under skin and in cavity. For beer-can method: open a room-temp beer, set can in cavity, stand bird on indirect zone.

steps.title: Grill indirect then crisp
steps.instruction: Run grill 375°F indirect with lid down until thickest part reads 165°F (60–75 minutes for a whole bird). Move to direct heat 5 minutes to crisp skin. Juices should run clear, not pink.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before carving. Jerk Chicken stays juicier if you don't slice immediately. Hold quarters on sheet trays at 180°F for late eaters.

steps.title: Carve for the line
steps.instruction: Quarter birds or slice thighs. Serve on sheet trays with pan juices — backup bird stays whole in a 180°F oven up to 25 minutes.

proTips: Use thighs — they forgive the grill and stay juicy.
Keep extra lime at the end of the line.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Jerk Chicken with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Jerk Chicken on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Island heat that still feeds eight. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
